somatostatin converts high affinity binding sites for oxotremorin-M-acetate to low affinity binding sites for the same agonist in rat brain.
somatostatin converted muscarinic receptors from high to low affinity binding sites in the hippocampal and cerebral cortex.

the effect of somastotatin on muscarinergic receptors and we found out that somatostatin converted high affinity binding sites for oxotremorin-M-acetate in the hippocampus, cortex and striatum to low affinity sites.
the effect of somastatin (SS) on muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (mAChR) in rat brain.
the effects of somatostain (SRIF) on muscarinic acetylcholine receptors (mAchRs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
somatostatin is able to convert M1 receptors to low affinity state, but not to M2 receptors.
the effect of somato-statin on mAchRs is selective to high affinity sites of M1 type.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
somatostatin is a potent antagonist of muscarinic receptors, but the effect is selective to M1 receptors.
somatostatin is a negative allosteric modulator of the high affinity binding site of the M1 mAchR.
somatostatin may be an endogenous modulator of mAchRs in the brain, and that the effect of somatastatin on mAchR may be selective to M1 receptors in the hippocampus, cerebral cortex, and striatum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
somatostatin may modulate the M1 receptor function in the brain.
somatostatin can alter the pharmacology of M1 mAchR, but not M2 mAchR.
somatostatin is not a selective inhibitor of muscarinic receptors and the effect of somastotin on muscarinic receptor function is dependent on the type of muscarinic receptor.
